response.sql:
WITH district_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    d.district_id,
    d.A3 as region,
    COUNT(a.account_id) as account_count
  FROM district d
  LEFT JOIN account a ON d.district_id = a.district_id
  GROUP BY d.district_id, d.A3
),
region_averages AS (
  SELECT 
    region,
    AVG(account_count) as region_avg
  FROM district_counts
  GROUP BY region
),
above_average_districts AS (
  SELECT 
    dc.district_id,
    dc.region,
    dc.account_count,
    dc.account_count - ra.region_avg as amount_above_avg
  FROM district_counts dc
  INNER JOIN region_averages ra ON dc.region = ra.region
  WHERE dc.account_count > ra.region_avg
),
global_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(account_count) as avg_count
  FROM above_average_districts
)
SELECT 
  aad.district_id,
  aad.region,
  aad.account_count,
  aad.amount_above_avg,
  aad.account_count / ga.avg_count as ratio
FROM above_average_districts aad
CROSS JOIN global_avg ga
ORDER BY ratio DESC
LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Districts with zero accounts are included in region average calculations. LEFT JOIN from district to account includes all districts in the district table, even those with no accounts. Region average = AVG(account_count) over all districts in the region.

alternatives.interpretation: Use INNER JOIN to exclude districts with zero accounts from region average calculations. Only districts with at least one account contribute to the region average, raising the threshold for 'above average' status.
